The Iberian Peninsula, the western Mediterranean, and the North African coast can be seen; the graticule marks meridians such as 20°W, 0°, and 20°E, as well as the approximately 41°N latitude line. Points A and B are located near the southern part of the Iberian Peninsula, basically distributed in the east-west direction, and their latitudes are both close to 40°—41°N, with a very small latitude difference. Then reason: estimating from the graticule in the figure, A is about at 8°W and B is about at 1°E, so the longitude difference between the two points is about 9°. Since the latitude difference is relatively small, the distance can be approximately calculated as an east-west distance at the same latitude.
